text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Swedish inventor Hakan Lans has received a leading aerospace industry prize, the Flight Aerospace Industry Award, for his new technology to develop a new communications and navigation system.
- Mining and rubber group Trelleborg is planning to buy companies worth 10 billion crowns in the next few years, according to a presentation at a company seminar.

- Swedish households are on the way to increasiong their private incomes and reducing dependency on social benefits, ending a negative trend, according to a report by the Swedish Employers' Confederation.
- Sweden gets its own home in St Petersburg with Prime Minister Goran Persson opening Sweden House on Wednesday.

- The average age of board members in Swedish listed companies is 59 despite a number of younger people joining the upper ranks of the business world in recent years. Five percent of board members are women and six percent from outside Sweden.

- International investment bank Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB) is engaged in advanced negotiations to buy Swedish property worth over four billion crowns from Vasakronan, a state-owned real estate company.

- Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson will today official inaugurate "Swedish House" in St Petersburg, an office and apartment building which was built to attract Swedish corporations to Russia. Financing was backed by the Swedish state but it has been harder than expected to find tennants for the complex with rents of 4,900 crowns per square metre.
- Sicilian start-up operator Med Airlines has placed an order for two Saab 200 aircraft and options on two more. The first delivery is due for November 1997 and the second in March 1998.
